thread:
Maya Rivera: heads up — AcmeInc reports p95/p99 regressions starting ~08:22 UTC. They see long tail latencies and a bunch of 429/401s that look like admission throttling + auth failures. queue depth in logs spikes.
Sam Patel: pinging eng-runtime, can you surface any admission-control changes? any recent rollout? :eyes:
Jin Park: not aware of a rollout. checking scheduler and admission metrics now, grabbing cluster dmesg and proxy logs.
Ellie Zhao: I can pull their tenant trace. which tenant id? saw increased retries from them in the last hour.
Maya Rivera: tenant: acme-prod-42. customer says it started after a low-volume bulk job at ~08:15 UTC. they also attached a repro curl that intermittently returns 401 then 429.
Acme Inc Support: we ran a batch export at 08:14, then started seeing failures across our app. repro attached. happy to let you hit staging or provide traces.
Sam Patel: ok thx. Jin, any obvious worker OOMs or eviction? devops-bot, any autoscaler activity?
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated queue_depth and admission_rejections for tenants matching "acme-prod-42" (8:21–08:30 UTC). Paging eng-runtime, eng-sre.
devops-bot: autoscaler scaled +2 nodes at 08:20 due to CPU; restart count on runtime-worker-7 is 0. no deploys recorded in window. (config: adm_max_concurrency=200, adm_window_ms=1000)
Jin Park: past-minute snapshot: worker-concurrency peaked, KV cache hit ratio fell ~15%, request bursts caused admission rejects. Also seeing many upstream auth 500->client 401 translations — looks like token validation service (auth-svc) returned 500 for some calls then we translated to 401 because of missing header. grabbing auth-svc logs.
Ellie Zhao: showing a chain: acme client -> gateway -> auth-svc -> runtime. auth-svc had intermittent DB timeouts around 08:19–08:23 (pg connections saturated). that caused auth validation timeouts; gateway treated them as auth failures which retried, causing pileup.
Maya Rivera: ok so primary: auth-svc degradation caused retries and a burst; secondary: admission + worker saturation turned pileup into 429s. priority is to stabilize customer and reduce pileup. suggested mitigations?
Sam Patel: immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase admission window to allow more inflight for acme-prod-42 (route-level override) 2) enable 503 fast-fail on auth-timeout path to avoid retries, 3) per-tenant rate-limit rollback if any aggressive client-side retry is happening.
Jin Park: running a route patch now to increase adm_max_concurrency for tenant acme-prod-42 from 200->350 and adm_window_ms 1000->1500. applying canary on two workers.
Ellie Zhao: also flipping gateway to treat auth-svc timeout as 503 (so client retries/backoff preferred) — pushing config change to gateway for tenant route.
Maya Rivera: please post commands & timestamps. I'll notify Acme support to throttle their client retries and gather repro.
Jin Park: applied canary 08:33 UTC to worker-pool-2. monitor link: https://console/redwood/monitoring/tenants/acme-prod-42/queue_depth
Jin Park: quick check logs (snippet):
```
2026-02-12T08:19:46Z runtime-worker-2 INFO admit_request tenant=acme-prod-42 depth=18 inflight=198 -> reject
2026-02-12T08:20:03Z auth-svc ERROR pg: timeout: pool exhausted
2026-02-12T08:20:05Z gateway WARN upstream auth-svc timeout -> returning 401
2026-02-12T08:20:06Z runtime-worker-5 INFO admit_request tenant=acme-prod-42 depth=3 inflight=210 -> accept
```
Sam Patel: observed immediate improvement in 5m window: p95 dropped ~300ms, p99 down ~1.2s. auth 500->401 conversion reduced after gateway change.
Acme Inc Support: we still see occasional 401s but much fewer. will keep client retries at backoff. thanks for the quick patch.
Maya Rivera: next steps: 1) eng-ml/infra to investigate auth-svc DB connection leak (Jin assigned) 2) eng-runtime to evaluate permanent per-tenant admission adjustments and guardrails (Sam & Ellie) 3) support to coordinate with customer on longer-term retry/backoff changes (Maya)
Jin Park: opened ticket INFRA-9274 for auth-svc PG pool sizing & query slow traces. timeline: investigate today, rollback/patch 24–48h.
Ellie Zhao: we'll add a per-tenant soft-cap that temporarily expands concurrency on observed short-lived bursts up to x2 but with circuit-breaker to avoid cascading. planning doc link: https://wiki/redwood/rt/per-tenant-admit
Maya Rivera: closing this thread for now — monitoring for 1h. if regressions reappear, we'll escalate to SEV. tagging oncall-bot and devops-bot for automated followups. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: MONITORING RULE: tenant_acme-prod-42.queue_depth > 10 sustained 5m — alerting channel eng-oncall and support.
